limitations: Unsupported Linux amd64 through Rosetta; no native-performance conversion or product ranking.
Fixed case order, cache history, compilation, host IO/thermal conditions and the additional A instance prevent causal isolation of state effects.
Three samples per cell provide descriptive statistics only.
Quiet static fixture; service budget remains UNAVAILABLE.
Sch-S and CPU/IO/version-retention costs remain; sparse observations do not establish absence of every short-lived lock.
No generalization to TDE, LOB, compression, arbitrary100-column schemas, HA or failover.
Aggregate acceptance and commit/push verification remain separate from this independent engineer review.

betterMethods: Use existing metadata or a suitable existing count/cache when approximate or previously established values meet the requirement.

For a required scan, inspect available narrow indexes and the selected plan. This experiment supports the observed fixture comparison without recommending production index creation or forcing an index.
designCoverage: The focused six-cell design covers B's three index conditions and A/B/C/D on the common composite structure.
Actual readable-secondary construction, static-rowset provenance, per-sample cold proofs, connection ownership, completion and teardown are covered independently.
engineerObjections: Controller1 cannot establish a successful zero-exit all run. The evidence and both reviewed documents preserve this distinction while independently establishing18 completed commands, normal SQL exits, logical cleanup and later same-criterion capacity recovery.
Estimated plans and index catalogs cannot establish every runtime access or lock. The report consistently describes planned indexes and retains actual sparse lock observations.
fastCount: The existing narrow-index fixture has substantially smaller planned-index capacity and lower observed latency than the clustered-only fixture.
D's lower observed latency does not make its result exact under writes or establish a globally faster safe method.
lockFactors: Actual observations include OBJECT/METADATA Sch-S and DATABASE S locks; NOLOCK and versioning do not remove schema or resource contention.
Lock flags and escalation settings are recorded without interpreting their presence as proof that COUNT takes shared row/table data locks.
omissions: No indispensable pending experiment identified within the authorized design.
Native hardware, write-time NOLOCK accuracy, production SLOs and broader schema matrices remain disclosed limitations.
